hints: Focus on what each property tells you, conductivity points to how metallic an element is, while melting point points to structure and bonding.
In Period 3, only silicon has a very high melting point because of its giant covalent structure, so it is a strong candidate for Y.
Pair that high melting point element with a good metallic conductor to its left and balance their ions to find the only formula that uses both.
walkthrough:
**Use conductivity to compare metallic character**

Good electrical conductivity means delocalised electrons and metallic bonding. So X must be more metallic, further to the left in Period 3, than Y.

Trend: $\text{Na, Mg, Al} > \text{Si} > \text{P, S, Cl}$ for conductivity

**Use melting point to spot the structure**

Melting point rises from Na to Al, then peaks sharply at Si, then falls sharply for P, S, Cl. Silicon is exceptional because it forms a giant covalent lattice.

Approximate m.p.: $\text{Mg} \approx 650^{\circ}\text{C} < \text{Si} \approx 1414^{\circ}\text{C}$

**Identify X and Y**

X conducts better than Y, so X is a metal. Y melts higher than X, so Y cannot be P, S or Cl which are simple molecular with low m.p. The only element that fits Y is silicon.

A metal to the left of Si, such as Mg, fits X perfectly: Mg conducts better than Si, but Si melts higher than Mg.

**Find the compound of X and Y**

We need a compound made from Mg and Si. Magnesium forms $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and silicon in silicides forms $\text{Si}^{4-}$.

Balancing charge:
$$2(+2) + (-4) = 0$$
So the formula is $\text{Mg}_2\text{Si}$.

options.A: MgS uses Mg and S. Mg does conduct better than S, but S has a much lower melting point (about 113 C) than Mg because it is simple molecular. This fails the second condition that Y melts higher than X.
options.B: Mg2Si uses Mg as X and Si as Y. Mg is a metal with high conductivity, Si is a metalloid with lower conductivity, so X conducts better. Si has giant covalent bonding with a very high melting point above Mg, so Y melts higher. Both conditions are satisfied.
options.C: NaCl uses Na and Cl. Na does conduct better than Cl, but Cl2 is a simple molecular gas/solid with a very low melting point, far below Na. This fails the condition that Y has the higher melting point.
options.D: SiCl4 uses Si and Cl. While Si conducts slightly better than Cl and melts higher than Cl, this would make Si the X and Cl the Y. Then Y (Cl) would have a lower melting point than X (Si), which is the opposite of what is required.
